quests.question: She argued ___ her flatmate about the chores.
quests.hint: 'Argue with someone' means to disagree in words.
quests.explanation: 'Argue with' a person and 'argue about' a topic. Here the preposition refers to the person she argued with.

quests.question: He believes strongly ___ the power of education.
quests.hint: 'Believe in' means to have faith or trust in something.
quests.explanation: 'Believe in' means to have faith or conviction: believe in yourself, believe in change.

quests.question: She concentrated ___ her breathing to calm down.
quests.hint: 'Concentrate on' means to focus your attention.
quests.explanation: 'Concentrate on' is the correct collocation: concentrate on the task, concentrate on your work.

quests.question: He has been dealing ___ a lot of stress lately.
quests.hint: 'Deal with' means to handle or manage a situation.
quests.explanation: 'Deal with' means to manage or handle something difficult: deal with a problem, deal with pressure.

quests.question: She insists ___ doing everything herself.
quests.hint: 'Insist on' is the fixed verb-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Insist on' means to demand firmly: insist on quality, insist on punctuality.

quests.question: They rely ___ solar power for all their electricity.
quests.hint: 'Rely on' means to depend on.
quests.explanation: 'Rely on' means to trust or depend on: rely on technology, rely on a colleague.

quests.question: He was staring ___ the screen for hours.
quests.hint: 'Stare at' means to look fixedly at something.
quests.explanation: 'Stare at' means to look intently: stare at the screen, stare at a painting.

quests.question: She apologised ___ being late to the meeting.
quests.hint: 'Apologise for' is the correct verb-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Apologise for' + noun or gerund: apologise for the delay, apologise for interrupting.

quests.question: He complained ___ his manager about the workload.
quests.hint: 'Complain to someone' (about something) is the correct pattern.
quests.explanation: 'Complain to' specifies the person receiving the complaint. 'Complain about' specifies the issue.

quests.question: She succeeded ___ passing all her exams.
quests.hint: 'Succeed in' is the correct verb-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Succeed in' is used with goals or activities: succeed in business, succeed in passing an exam.

quests.question: He disagrees ___ his colleagues on most issues.
quests.hint: 'Disagree with someone' is the fixed collocation.
quests.explanation: 'Disagree with' a person is the standard form. 'Disagree about' is also possible with a topic.

quests.question: She decided to invest ___ property.
quests.hint: 'Invest in' is the standard verb-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Invest in' means to put money or effort into something: invest in property, invest in training.

quests.question: He has struggled ___ confidence all his life.
quests.hint: 'Struggle with' means to have difficulty with something.
quests.explanation: 'Struggle with' describes persistent difficulty: struggle with anxiety, struggle with maths.

quests.question: She spoke ___ a nervous voice during the presentation.
quests.hint: 'In a (type of) voice' is the correct pattern.
quests.explanation: 'In a voice' describes the manner of speaking: in a loud voice, in a whisper, in a nervous voice.

quests.question: He is coping ___ the pressure remarkably well.
quests.hint: 'Cope with' means to manage a difficult situation.
quests.explanation: 'Cope with' means to handle successfully: cope with stress, cope with change, cope with loss.

quests.question: The prize money will be divided ___ the three winners.
quests.hint: 'Among' is used when sharing between three or more people.
quests.explanation: 'Among' is used when dividing between three or more parties. 'Between' is used for exactly two.

quests.question: This is strictly ___ you and me.
quests.hint: 'Between you and me' is a fixed expression for two people sharing a secret.
quests.explanation: 'Between' is used for two people or parties: between you and me, a deal between two companies.

quests.question: The salary was distributed ___ the entire department.
quests.hint: 'Among' is used when distributing to more than two.
quests.explanation: 'Among the entire department' uses 'among' because there are many people involved, not just two.

quests.question: The plane flew ___ an altitude of 10,000 metres.
quests.hint: 'At an altitude' is the correct expression for height above ground.
quests.explanation: 'At an altitude of' is the fixed expression: fly at an altitude of, cruise at an altitude of.

quests.question: The eagle soared ___ the valley below.
quests.hint: 'Above' describes a position directly higher, without movement across.
quests.explanation: 'Above the valley' means at a higher level. 'Over' implies passing across: flying over the valley from one side to the other.

quests.question: The temperature dropped ___ freezing point.
quests.hint: 'Below freezing point' means a temperature lower than 0°C.
quests.explanation: 'Below' describes a position at a lower level or value: below zero, below average, below the surface.

quests.question: She reached ___ the top of the class.
quests.hint: 'Reach the top' - but 'at the top of the class' is the location.
quests.explanation: 'At the top of the class' describes her position in the academic ranking. 'Reach' takes a direct object.

quests.question: He spoke ___ behalf of the whole team.
quests.hint: 'On behalf of' is a fixed prepositional phrase.
quests.explanation: 'On behalf of' means representing or acting for another person or group.

quests.question: She passed the driving test ___ her third attempt.
quests.hint: 'On your first/second/third attempt' is the correct expression.
quests.explanation: 'On her third attempt' uses 'on' - this is the fixed preposition with numbered attempts.

quests.question: He threw the ball ___ the window by accident.
quests.hint: 'Through the window' means going through the glass.
quests.explanation: 'Through' means passing within and out of something: throw something through the window means breaking the glass.

quests.question: She leaned ___ the fence to talk to her neighbour.
quests.hint: 'Lean against' means to rest your body on a surface.
quests.explanation: 'Lean against' describes resting against a surface: lean against the wall, lean against the door.

quests.question: He pushed the boxes ___ the corner of the room.
quests.hint: 'Into the corner' shows movement toward and into a position.
quests.explanation: 'Into the corner' describes movement that ends at the corner. 'In the corner' would describe the location only.

quests.question: She has been off work ___ a cold.
quests.hint: 'Off work with an illness' means absent due to that illness.
quests.explanation: 'Off work with' a cold or illness means you are absent because of it: off sick with flu, off work with a back problem.

quests.question: He sat ___ the back of the classroom.
quests.hint: 'At the back' refers to a position in the rear area.
quests.explanation: 'At the back' describes a position in the rearmost area: at the back of the room, at the front of the queue.

quests.question: She is involved ___ three different projects.
quests.hint: 'Involved in' is the correct adjective-preposition combination.
quests.explanation: 'Involved in' means participating in or connected with: involved in a project, involved in research.
